hits.hook: every single article i've written with 1M+ views wasn't actually written by me...
hits.original_en:
every single article i've written with 1M+ views wasn't actually written by me...

i just used my phone to dictate it

because the truth is... your brain doesn't think in text

it never did, it thinks in connections, in patterns, in half-formed ideas that make perfect sense until you try to type them out

and the moment your fingers hit a keyboard, you stop thinking and start performing because every sentence gets filtered through "does this sound good?"

so i started using tools like Wispr Flow or Willow to dictate all my first drafts... here's what my process looks like now:

> i go for a walk, open the app on my phone
> talk through the entire article like i'm explaining it to someone who asked a great question
> the app captures it all in real time, cleans out the filler words, formats it into actual paragraphs
> 15 minutes later i have a draft on my phone that reads like something i'd publish, not a messy transcript i need to spend an hour cleaning up

then i work on the the structure, ask claude for refinements, rewrite some parts and publish... that's a full article, under 2 hours

when you speak, you don't overthink

that directness hits different because readers can feel it... there's a natural rhythm in spoken thought that you cannot recreate by typing carefully (unless you're absolutely cracked at copywriting)

been running this system on desktop and iphone for months, highly recommend
hits.draft_en:
how to draft a 1M+ view long-form X article on a 15-minute walk without staring at a blank keyboard

the moment your fingers touch a keyboard your brain switches from explaining an idea to performing like a textbook

use these 4 voice dictation workflows with your favorite transcription models instead

> write 3 bullet questions on your phone lock screen before you step outside
> open Wispr Flow or Willow on a 15-minute walk and explain the answers out loud like you are talking to 1 smart friend
> drop the raw transcript into Claude Code with `voice_cleanup.md` to strip filler words while keeping 9k characters of your natural phrasing intact
> add line breaks and 1 concrete screenshot at your desk before publishing
hits.video_tip: 45s mobile + desktop split-screen: record a 15-minute walk dictating into Wispr Flow on your phone, then show `voice_clean.md` formatting it into a long-form article.

hits.hook: I think the startup world has made fundraising way too much of a full-time job.
hits.original_en:
I think the startup world has made fundraising way too much of a full-time job.

Founders spend six months pitching 100 VCs, tweaking decks, chasing introductions, and answering the same questions over and over.

Then they finally raise $5M, celebrate for a week, and start preparing for the next round.

At some point, when do you actually build the company?

I’ve seen founders who are incredible at raising money but surprisingly average at running a business.

Fundraising is an important skill, but it’s not the business.

Your job isn’t to convince investors you’re building something valuable.

It’s to actually build something valuable.

The best fundraising strategy is having a business investors can’t ignore.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
